title: Connector onboarding runbook and SLA bakeoff
content:
Purpose and scope:
This runbook is intended to guide engineering and security teams through enterprise customer onboarding for SIEM export connectors (Splunk, Datadog, Azure Sentinel). It focuses on three combined concerns: mapping RBAC v2 audit semantics to customer SIEM roles, defining the audit log schema and evidence automation hooks customers expect, and running an SLA/bakeoff verification before production cutover.

Status and audience:
- Draft operational runbook for Engineering, SRE, Security, and Solutions Engineering.
- Assumes basic connector implementation exists (HTTP/HTTPS forwarder, retry/backoff, auth token rotation).

High-level checklist (quick start):
1) Engage customer security + platform: confirm required fields, retention window, and PII rules.
2) Provide sample event envelopes and field map for review.
3) Run acceptance tests (see test matrix).
4) Run SLA bakeoff (latency/throughput/burst).
5) Enable evidence automation hooks and verify alerting/round-trip evidence.
6) Sign off and schedule production cutover.

RBAC v2 -> SIEM role mapping guidance:
- Goal: Ensure events retain actor identity and role context but do not expose internal IDs that violate tenant isolation.
- Map RBAC v2 fields to SIEM as follows (recommended minimal set):
  * actor.id -> user.id
  * actor.display_name -> user.name
  * actor.roles -> user.roles (comma-separated)
  * resource.type -> object.type
  * resource.id (redact if PII) -> object.id
  * action -> event.action (use kebab-case)
  * outcome -> event.outcome (success|failure|denied)
  * request_id -> event.request_id
  * timestamp -> @timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC)

- Privacy note: If a customer requires strict redaction, provide a redaction profile that replaces resource.id and any email-like actor identifiers with hashed tokens and include a mapping proof artifact only provided under legal request.

Audit log schema and event envelope (canonical example):
- Keep envelopes compact. Consumers expect: timestamp, service, event, actor, object, request_id, metadata.
- Example canonical envelope (customer-facing sample, not for transport as-is):

  {
    "@timestamp": "2026-02-15T22:13:02Z",
    "service": "redwood-inference",
    "event": {
      "action": "model.deploy",
      "outcome": "success",
      "request_id": "req_8f3d2a"
    },
    "actor": {
      "id": "u_12345",
      "display_name": "jane.doe@example.com",
      "roles": "admin,model-owner"
    },
    "object": {
      "type": "model",
      "id": "my-model-prod-v2"
    },
    "metadata": {
      "region": "us-west-2",
      "env": "prod"
    }
  }

- Transport: most connectors use batched JSON lines (NDJSON) over HTTPS with Content-Type: application/x-ndjson. For Splunk HTTP Event Collector (HEC) wrap per-Hec event fields; for Datadog use API-specific envelope. Provide a translation shim where necessary.

Evidence automation hooks:
- Purpose: allow customers to automatically capture supporting artifacts (config snapshots, policy decisions, KL-snapshots) when specific audit events occur.
- Recommended approach: include evidence pointer fields in the event: evidence_url (pre-signed short-lived), evidence_hash (sha256), evidence_type (snapshot|config|policy-decision).
- Hooks to validate: on event with evidence_url present, SIEM should be able to fetch artifact within TTL and validate hash. Run tests that intentionally corrupt one byte to ensure hash verification fails (negative test).

Connector acceptance test matrix (minimum passing criteria):
1) Functional correctness
   - Field parity: sample events show mapping completeness (>= 90% of required fields).
   - Redaction policy: PII redaction profile applied as requested.
2) Throughput and latency
   - Steady-state throughput: sustain 1000 events/s for the agreed tenant size without dropped events.
   - P99 end-to-end latency (ingest to SIEM indexing): <= 800ms for Splunk HEC in our test region; adjust per-customer baseline.
3) Resilience and backpressure
   - Connector implements exponential backoff with jitter for 429/503 and maintains a bounded disk-backed buffer of at least 10 minutes of traffic at peak rate.
4) Delivery semantics
   - At-least-once delivery with idempotency key (event.request_id) support.
5) Evidence validation
   - Evidence artifacts are reachable and hash-verified within TTL.

SLA/bakeoff plan (how we run it):
- Prep: coordinate maintenance window with customer technical contact. Ensure test indices and API keys created in customer SIEM.
- Ramp phases:
  1) Sanity (10 rps) for schema validation.
  2) Mid (200 rps) for throughput and partial failure injection.
  3) Peak (configured target, e.g., 1k rps) sustained for 10 minutes.
  4) Burst test (10x peak for 60s) to validate backpressure.
- Metrics to capture: ingestion latency histogram, 4xx/5xx counts, retry rate, buffer growth, disk-buffer spill events.
- Success criteria: no data loss observed in customer test index, retries lead to eventual ingestion, p99 latency within agreed SLO.

Failure modes and mitigations (operational notes):
- 429/503 from SIEM: trigger exponential backoff, alert SRE; if persisted >5m, toggle fallback to lower-fidelity envelope (drop metadata fields) as configured per customer.
- Network partition: the connector should persist to disk with monotonic ordering guarantees, and resume replay after connectivity restored.
- Partial indexing (some fields missing): prioritize non-PII core fields (timestamp, action, request_id, outcome) and mark others as optional. Provide repair job to rehydrate missing fields where possible.

Customer configuration options (negotiable during onboarding):
- Retention window for events on our side before we purge buffered copies (default 21 days).
- Redaction profile (none | email-hash | full-hash | custom regex).
- Evidence TTL (default 7 days pre-signed link).
- Delivery mode (push vs pull).

Operational runbook (step-by-step for cutover):
1) Confirm credentials and test indices with customer.
2) Flip to test API key and run Sanity phase. Inspect first 100 events in SIEM.
3) Run Mid and Peak phases. Check buffer metrics and retry behavior.
4) Validate evidence artifacts for a sample of events (fetch and hash).
5) Present results (latency histograms, error rates) to customer.
6) Agree on SLA terms and schedule production cutover.
7) Post-cutover: 24h high-touch monitoring and daily report for first week.

Acceptance checklist (to obtain sign-off):
- [ ] Field parity validated (customer ack)
- [ ] Redaction profile applied and tested
- [ ] Evidence artifacts validated
- [ ] Latency & throughput meet agreed SLOs
- [ ] Backpressure behavior validated under burst
- [ ] No critical 5xx/error persistent trend after 1 hour
- [ ] Cutover runbook documented in customer Confluence

Open questions / TODOs (for solutions engineering and product):
- Should we standardize a single evidence artifact storage pattern across customers? pros/cons (cost/latency/privacy).
- Decide canonical minimal event schema v1.1 and deprecation timeline for older envelopes.
- Add telemetry hooks for ``evidence_fetch_failures`` to product metrics.

Appendix: Helpful commands and test vectors
- Example curl to send an NDJSON batch (replace HEC/API key):
  curl -X POST "https://siem.example.com/ingest" \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/x-ndjson' \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer TEST_KEY' \
    --data-binary $'{"@timestamp":"2026-02-15T22:13:02Z","service":"redwood","event":{"action":"model.deploy","outcome":"success","request_id":"req_1"}}
{"@timestamp":"2026-02-15T22:13:03Z","service":"redwood","event":{"action":"model.update","outcome":"success","request_id":"req_2"}}'

- Minimal negative test: send event with evidence_url that points to 1-byte-corrupted artifact and ensure hash mismatch is detected.

Notes to self:
- Coordinate with legal on evidence retention contracts for regulated customers (HIPAA/GDPR constraints).
- File a small RFC to finalize canonical schema and publish as product contract.

Document history:
- 2025-11-03: initial draft (Aisha)
- 2025-12-10: added evidence automation section (Marcus)
- 2026-02-20: updated bakeoff thresholds and acceptance criteria (Priya)
